audience_knows_before: The world is private and the cave was previously empty.
audience_expects_before: An intruder, anomaly or forgotten construction may explain it.

question_or_fact: Is the destination the same world at another time?
audience_knows_before: A portal normally implies another dimension within the story’s Minecraft language.
audience_expects_before: The other side may be the Nether, a copy or a ruined future.
character_knowledge_before: The protagonist expects an unfamiliar destination.
audience_knows_after: Matched geography and then the visible younger self establish one location at different times.
audience_expects_after: The audience expects participation in a fixed history rather than parallel worlds.
notes: Spatial proof arrives before explicit temporal interpretation.

question_or_fact: Can an intervention create a different past?
audience_knows_before: The protagonist has not yet acted in the earlier state.
audience_expects_before: A warning may permit a corrected version.
character_knowledge_before: He still hopes the second crossing is another chance.
audience_knows_after: The wool marker he lays is the same marker he already remembers.
audience_expects_after: Further interventions are expected to become causes of observed details.
notes: The warning fails because it is incomplete and ambiguous, not because a force erases it.

question_or_fact: Who made the red wool marker?

audience_expects_before: It may be irrelevant decoration or another player’s warning.
audience_knows_after: His travelling self takes local wool and lays the incomplete route.
audience_expects_after: The audience now examines other familiar irregularities as self-authored clues.
notes: The wool has a local material origin and is not carried into a closed object loop.

question_or_fact: Why does the portal match his own habits?
audience_knows_before: Footing, torch and geometry have been shown but not uniquely attributed.
audience_expects_before: A knowledgeable stranger or temporal echo may be responsible.
character_knowledge_before: He increasingly suspects he must reproduce the frame.
audience_knows_after: He physically mines the obsidian, creates the footing, places the torch and watches his younger self enter.
audience_expects_after: The remaining suspense moves from builder identity to the cost of his construction.
notes: The confirmation is an action match rather than an explanatory monologue.

audience_knows_after: Fire traces from contained lava through his staging into the connected timber stair.
audience_expects_after: The audience expects the known ruin but not necessarily total relational loss.
notes: Exact Minecraft behaviour remains conditional on version testing.

question_or_fact: Did the wolf die in the fire?
audience_knows_before: The aftermath showed an empty open pen without remains or direct death evidence.
audience_expects_before: Loss is feared, while escape remains logically possible.
character_knowledge_before: The protagonist initially treats the absence as likely loss.

audience_expects_after: The audience expects the final angle to explain why the earlier self did not see it.
notes: The narration may express fear but must never assert death.

audience_expects_after: The audience can reconstruct why the earlier self chased and crossed again.
notes: Use the exact crouch count, torch side and camera line from SC-04.

question_or_fact: Did any event repeat or change outcome?
audience_knows_before: Several states of the same place could initially resemble retries.
audience_expects_before: The protagonist hopes foreknowledge produces a revised fire.
character_knowledge_before: He gradually recognises his remembered interventions.
audience_knows_after: One world chronology accounts for marker, portal, fire, rescue and silhouette; the ruin is unchanged.
audience_expects_after: No reset or branch is expected after the portal is extinguished.
notes: Repeated compositions are viewpoints on single events, not repeated events.

question_or_fact: Where did the portal’s temporal routing first originate?
audience_knows_before: The physical frame has ordinary materials but behaves unlike an ordinary portal.
audience_expects_before: The builder reveal may also explain the anomaly’s first cause.
character_knowledge_before: The protagonist only knows the route empirically and copies the remembered arrangement.
audience_knows_after: He made the frame, but no external first design for its temporal pattern is supplied.

notes: Human approval is required before treating this open causal-information loop as canon.
